Hariom Paswan @ Tulsi vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:163835
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 8767 of 2023

Applicant :- Hariom Paswan @ Tulsi
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Hari Bans Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Pankaj Tripathi, learned A.G.A. for the State and
perused the record.

2.  This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant Hariom Paswan @ Tulsi seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 01 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and under Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Bhanwarkol, District- Ghazipur.
3.

The prosecution story as alleged in the FIR is that on 24.4.2018 the deceased was married with the present applicant but she was subjected to cruelty and harassment for demand of additional dowry by her in-laws and subsequently her unnatural death by way of hanging was caused on 1.1.2023.
FIR was lodged on 2.1.2023 and investigation started, which is going on.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has no concern with the present matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
It is further argued that investigation is going-on and till date no charge-sheet has been submitted against the accused applicant.

It is further submitted that the accused applicant who is the husband of the deceased works at Dubai as aluminium fitter in Mathews Methal MFG. L.L.C. and he was not Hariom Paswan @ Tulsi vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161733935/
1 present at the place of occurrence when the incident occurred.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that he is passport holder from 5.11.2012 which was renewed on 7.9.2022 and a residential Visa was also issued by U.A.E. Government in his favour for doing his job there.
It is further submitted that the applicant came from Dubai to Mumbai on 6.7.2023 after a long time of the occurrence.
It is also submitted that as per post mortem report no ante mortem injury except ligature mark has been found over the body of the deceased.

It is further submitted that the deceased was not happy with the applicant on account of his body structure and beauty and that is why she was living in a state of depression where under she committed suicide.
It is further submitted that as a matter of fact the marriage of the deceased had taken place with the applicant on 24.10.2013 and in 2018 gauna was held and in 2019 a male child was born.
It is further submitted that the applicant has been cooperative with the investigation of the case and is entitled for anticipatory bail.
It has been submitted that in case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

It is submitted that the applicant is the husband of the deceased and ample evidence has been collected against him during the course of investigation so far as to he was the main person who demanded additional dowry from the deceased for construction of house and for his foreign trip and caused harassment and cruelty to her.

It is further submitted that the death of the deceased has been occurred in her matrimonial home and the cause of death has been found asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging but the absence of the accused from the scene of occurrence does not go to help him at this stage.
It is also submitted that plea of alibi has been taken by the accused applicant cannot be taken into account at the stage of considering the anticipatory bail application.

6. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences,
the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

7. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, I deem it not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
Prayer made in the application is refused.
8. The anticipatory bail application is rejected.

Order Date :- 11.8.2023//Fhd  Hariom Paswan @ Tulsi vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161733935/
